en: Now then you got 2 main commands you have or
2 main methods you have to interact with the
database.
You have db.run
and you have db.query.
And both can be used for executing SQL
commands. But the idea is that you use
db.run for one-off commands like here where
I ensure that I have a notes table if it
doesn't exist yet.
Whereas db.query is meant for reusable
commands because when you use db.query, a
cached statement will be created behind the
scenes, which is simply a statement that's a
bit faster and more optimized to execute, so
to say. So you should use the db.query
method for your query commands where you
fetch data from the database, which are
typically executed a lot, and db.run for
these one-off commands or tasks,
which is why I'm using db.run here
to enable WAL mode, and that's just a
configuration command which you should
basically execute every time you're working
with SQLite. It just gives you better
performance, and there really is no reason
to not use WAL mode. It's just not the
default for historic reasons.
Then again, as mentioned here, I'm executing
a statement to create a notes table,
and then I also create an index.
Then here, these commands are executed to
ensure that whenever the database connection
is closed,
these extra files here are cleaned up. These
are extra files that are created because of
that vol mode, and if that code weren't
here, they would persist if I stop this
application.
That's not necessarily a problem, but I'd
like to have a clean file system. So with my
setup, if I shut the server down, you see
those files disappeared.
